The code never strips trailing zeroes. It unconditionally returns DecimalNode.valueOf(v) with the value as provided, and the inline comment explicitly states normalization is now up to the caller ('it's now up to caller to do normalization, if any; we will construct node with given value'). The documented normalization behavior is not implemented at all in this method, regardless of how the factory was configured.
doc_conflicts.doc_value:
In the event that the factory has been built to normalize decimal
values, the BigDecimal argument will be stripped off its trailing zeroes,
using {@link BigDecimal#stripTrailingZeros()}.
doc_conflicts.recommendation: حدّث التوثيق أو الكود لحتى يتطابقوا

The bracket notation '[Z|[+-]hh:mm]' marks the time-zone designator as optional, but the code requires one unconditionally: if the input ends after the date/time without 'Z' or a +/- offset, it throws (which is converted to a ParseException). A string matching the documented format with the optional zone omitted, e.g. '2011-01-01T10:20:30', therefore fails to parse, contradicting the documented format.
doc_conflicts.recommendation: حدّث التوثيق أو الكود لحتى يتطابقوا

The documentation states the chronology parameter must not be null, but the code routes the parameter through DateTimeUtils.getChronology, which accepts null and substitutes the default (ISO) chronology instead of rejecting it. Passing null therefore succeeds with a default chronology rather than being invalid as documented.

The documented format includes a time zone offset component ('ZZ', e.g. '+01:00' or 'Z'), but the code prints a LocalTime with ISODateTimeFormat.time(). LocalTime is a partial without any time zone, so the offset element of that formatter is never printed; the actual output is 'HH:mm:ss.SSS' (e.g. '10:20:30.400') with no offset suffix. The offset part of the documented format does not match what the method produces.
doc_conflicts.doc_value: Output the time in ISO8601 format (HH:mm:ss.SSSZZ).
doc_conflicts.recommendation: حدّث التوثيق أو الكود لحتى يتطابقوا
doc_conflicts.evidence: doc: "Output the time in ISO8601 format (HH:mm:ss.SSSZZ)." | code L3: "return ISODateTimeFormat.time().print(this);"

The documentation states the separator is output only if fields are printed AFTER it, but the code contradicts this: the method is named appendSeparatorIfFieldsBefore and it passes (true, false) as the use-before/use-after flags, meaning the separator is output only if fields BEFORE it are printed. The documentation's own example ('will only output the comma if the days field is output', where days precedes the separator) also describes 'before' semantics, showing the 'after' claim conflicts with both the code and the rest of the documentation.
doc_conflicts.doc_value: Append a separator, which is output only if fields are printed after the separator.
doc_conflicts.recommendation: حدّث التوثيق أو الكود لحتى يتطابقوا
doc_conflicts.evidence: doc: "Append a separator, which is output only if fields are printed after the separator." | code L2: "        return appendSeparator(text, text, true, false);"
